title: Tintin and Snowy.
lines: A young reporter lives in the city of Brussels.
His name is Tintin.
He has a tuft of hair that always sticks straight up, like a quiff.
That's why he looks the way he does.
Tintin writes stories for the newspaper.
True stories, about adventures all over the world.
Tintin has a little dog.
A little white dog with curly hair.
His name is Snowy.
Snowy is very clever and very brave.
He just loves bones a little too much.
One morning Tintin and Snowy are walking through the market.
It's a flea market, with old things.
Clocks, books, paintings, lamps.
Tintin sees a small, old ship.
A model of a sailing ship, with white sails and a wooden hull.
How lovely, says Tintin.
He buys the little ship for a few coins.
But as soon as he has bought it, two men come up to him.
They wear bowler hats and they look exactly the same.
They're the detectives Thomson and Thompson.
They work for the police.
Watch out, young man!
says Thomson.
There are pickpockets at the market!
To be precise, says Thompson, there are pickpockets at the market.
Tintin laughs.
They always say everything twice.
Then another man comes along.
He has a black hat and a dark coat.
He wants to buy the little ship.
I'll give you ten times as much money for it!
he says.
But Tintin doesn't want to sell.
Why does everyone want this little ship?
he thinks.
At home Tintin puts the ship on the cupboard.
Snowy sniffs it.
Woof!
Then the neighbours' cat jumps in.
Snowy runs after it.
They run around the table, over the chair, into the cupboard.
Crash!
The little ship falls on the floor.
The mast breaks.
And a little piece of paper rolls out of the mast.
Tintin picks it up.
It's a very old note.
Something is written on it, in old letters.
And there's a drawing on it.
A map!
A treasure map!
Look, Snowy!
says Tintin.
This is the way to a hidden treasure!
That's why everyone wanted the little ship!
That night Snowy hears something.
He pricks up his ears.
Grrr.
There's someone in the house!
It's the man with the black hat.
He's creeping towards the cupboard.
He's looking for the little ship.
Snowy jumps out of his basket.
Woof!
Woof!
Woof!
He bites the man's trouser leg.
The man yells.
Tintin turns on the light.
The man runs away, through the window.
But he loses his hat.
In the hat there's a little card.
It's the address of a big castle outside the city.
Tintin and Snowy go there.
They creep through the garden.
They look through the window.
Inside are the man with the black hat and his friends.
They have a little ship too.
Exactly the same!
And a piece of a map too!
There are three little ships, says the man.
And together they show the way to the treasure.
We already have two.
We still have to find the third one!
But Tintin has the third piece.
Now he knows.
He has to be quick.
He runs back home.
But the men have seen him.
They run after him.
Tintin jumps into a car.
Snowy jumps in after him.
They drive through the streets of Brussels.
Past the Atomium, with its big silver balls.
Past the Grand Place.
The men drive after them.
Then Tintin has an idea.
He drives to the police station.
Thomson and Thompson are standing there.
The men drive straight towards them and get caught.
Well done, Tintin!
says Thomson.
To be precise: very well done, says Thompson.
And the treasure?
Tintin looks at the three pieces of map.
They lead to an island, far away in the sea.
Snowy, says Tintin, what do you think?
Shall we go on an adventure?
Snowy wags his tail.
Woof!
But first he gets a big bone.
Because tonight he was the biggest hero of all.
The end.
